## Who Counts as Unemployed?

The unemployment rate is calculated using the number of unemployed people and the number of employed people—not everyone who lacks a job. Its denominator is the combined total of employed and unemployed people.

A person on temporary layoff who expects to be recalled may qualify as unemployed without actively searching for work. By contrast, someone whose only job-search activity was browsing listings does not meet the active-search requirement.

In general, a person must not have been employed during the survey’s reference week and must have been available for work, except in the case of temporary illness. They must also have actively searched for work during the four-week period ending with that reference week, unless they were temporarily laid off and expected recall. These conditions determine whether someone is counted among the unemployed—and included in the rate’s denominator.
